release_gate_R2: complete for server-side permissions acceptance; connected-client acceptance remains R3
cases: actual installed permission services for both aliases and six command nodes
real provider unset, grant, explicit deny with actual level-four operator entry, regrant and grant removal
cached command parse: time and online-name filter suggestions stop after revocation, including legacy player argument
recovery UUID suggestions stop after actual provider revocation
block/container lookup success and controlled storage failure callbacks emit no queued result/error packets after revocation
inspector permission loss disables access and queues one notice; revoked paging and deferred block/container callbacks emit no result/error packets
four read-only item observation types end after real provider revocation without item journals or result bursts
provider-free actual operator entries levels zero through four, then removal, via installed Fabric API fallback and NeoForge built-in handler

real SQLite block rollback: denied admission, revocation during planning, before claim, during claim, before apply, preservation of older PENDING row, authorized mutation/finalization, revocation after mutation before journal finalization
limitations: No network-connected player or client presentation was tested. Synthetic players used real permission attachments and unconnected packet listeners; outgoing packet queues were observed, not client rendering.
Fabric uses the installed LuckPerms initialization hook; NeoForge invokes the actual provider login listener. Full network login and unrelated pack login listeners remain in R3.
Controlled lookup storage failures use a private adapter; permission decisions are never mocked. Block rollback acceptance uses the actual SQLite backend and actual world states.
Read-only item checks cover permission cancellation before inventory/recovery results, not item apply or a new saved-state durability contract.
The Fabric baseline includes Fabric Permissions API nested in a required dependency. Provider-free acceptance verifies API fallback without LuckPerms, not a runnable pack without that API.

LuckPerms NeoForge 5.4.150 is listed for 1.21.4 but passed this 1.21.1 combination. NeoForge 5.4.140 reproduced the upstream capability failure; universal provider/pack compatibility is not certified.
